metaDescription: Six table reading lamps for end tables and side tables, compared on dimming, controls, charging and light quality for comfortable evening reading.
introParagraphs: A table reading lamp lives on the end table beside your armchair or on the side table by the sofa, and it has to light a book or tablet without lighting the whole room. This guide compares six lamps that fit that job: the BOHON with a rotary knob and auto dimming, the LEPOWER 800 lumen panel lamp, the TROND swipe dimmer, the Fitfull touch lamp with an AC outlet, the foldable Dott Arts lamp and the budget EJIAXIN gooseneck.

The spread across these six is wide. The BOHON uses 56 SMD LEDs across 3000K to 5500K, the TROND offers seven brightness levels through a swipe groove, the Dott Arts folds down on a 230 degree arm, and the Fitfull is the only one that adds an AC outlet next to USB-A and USB-C. The LEPOWER stands out on output with 800 lumens and 50 combined lighting choices, while the EJIAXIN is a plain, flexible forged iron lamp with no electronics to learn.

We evaluated these lamps from product specs and buyer feedback, weighing how pleasant the light is, how easy the controls are from a seated position, and how well each fits a crowded table. Older eyes need much more light than younger eyes for the same print, so lamps with generous dimming range and low glare ranked above those with fixed output.

products.name: BOHON LED Table Lamp with Rotary Knob and Auto Dimming
products.description:
The BOHON stands out because it pairs a physical rotary knob with sensible smart features. Fifty-six SMD2835 LEDs give a soft, non-flickering light across 3000K to 5500K, and a knob adjusts brightness while a key switch changes the color mode. A knob is easier to grip and read by feel than a touch sensor, which matters when you reach for it from a chair.

The intelligent induction mode senses ambient light and adjusts brightness automatically, and the memory function remembers your last setting. The tradeoff is that auto dimming can surprise you when someone turns on a nearby light, and having both a knob and a key switch means two controls to learn. There is no AC outlet, so charging is limited to the USB port.

Setup is just plugging in, and the knob is simple to wipe clean. Against the TROND, which uses a swipe groove, the BOHON is more forgiving for stiff fingers, and it is more affordable than the LEPOWER while still offering a wide color range. Keep the sensor window clear of dust and cups, since the auto mode reads room light through it. It makes a calm companion for an armchair beside a window.
products.bestFor: Armchair readers who prefer a real knob and gentle automatic dimming
pros: Rotary knob is easy to grip and use by feel
56 LEDs give soft, non-flickering light
Auto-dimming adapts to room light
Memory restores your last setting
cons: Two controls take a little learning
Auto-dim can react to nearby lights

products.name: LEPOWER 800 Lumen LED Table Lamp
products.description:
The LEPOWER is the strongest light in this group, with a 12W panel rated at 800 lumens and a wider panel than a typical lamp. It combines five color temperatures with ten brightness levels for 50 lighting options, and its RG0 rated beads are aimed at eye comfort. For dense print on a side table it gives the most headroom.

The tradeoff is complexity and footprint, because 50 modes are more than most people need and the wide panel takes up table space. Brightness this high can also be harsh in a dim room, so you will want to dial it down for evening use.

Ownership is easy with a plug-in cord and a stable base. In this comparison it is the pick for people who struggle to see print, while the BOHON offers a more relaxed, ambient glow. If you share the room, its wide panel is the one that is easiest to see in a dim corner. Dial it down in the evening so the panel does not look harsh.
products.bestFor: Readers who need extra brightness for fine print on a side table
pros: 800 lumens gives the most light in this group
Ten brightness levels across five colors
Wide panel spreads light evenly
RG0 rated beads for eye comfort
cons: Fifty modes are more than most readers need
Wide panel needs more table room

products.name: TROND Eye-Caring Table Lamp with Memory
products.description:
The TROND uses a surface light source and a light guide panel to create a flicker-free, anti-glare light that spreads evenly. Seven brightness levels are set by swiping a dimmer groove, three color modes are chosen by long-pressing the LED indicator, and a memory function stores your last setting.

The swipe groove is quick and satisfying once learned, but it needs a bit of finger accuracy, which is harder with stiff hands than a knob. The long-press mode change is also not obvious at first.

It is a plug-in lamp that sits neatly on a table and wipes clean easily. Compared with the Fitfull, which has charging ports, the TROND focuses entirely on the light quality and offers more brightness steps. Mind the top of the lamp, because swipe controls are easiest to use when the panel faces you. The even light makes it a good match for a side table in a living room.
products.bestFor: Readers who value even, glare-free light with fine brightness steps
pros: Light guide panel spreads light without glare
Seven brightness levels by swiping
Three color modes for day and evening
Memory recalls your preferred setting
cons: Swipe control needs some finger accuracy

products.name: Fitfull Touch Table Lamp with AC Outlet
products.description:
The Fitfull is the practical lamp for an end table that doubles as a charging spot. It has an AC outlet plus USB-A and USB-C ports, and a touch anywhere on its base or pole cycles through three brightness levels. That makes it easy to switch on without finding a button.

The tradeoff is that three levels is coarse compared with the TROND's seven or the LEPOWER's ten, and touch surfaces can trigger accidentally. It is better as a general reading lamp than for very fine print.

Setup is simple and the smooth body wipes clean. Compared with the BOHON, it is simpler to use and offers charging, but gives up the color range and auto dimming. The AC outlet means a small fan or a hearing aid charger can share the same wall socket. It is a practical pick when the end table is the only spot near an outlet.
products.bestFor: End tables that also need to charge a phone and plug in a small device
pros: AC outlet and two USB ports on the lamp
Touch anywhere makes switching on simple
Three brightness steps are easy to remember
cons: Touch surface can respond to bumps

products.name: Dott Arts Foldable LED Table Lamp with USB Ports
products.description:
The Dott Arts is a foldable touch lamp with five light colors and three brightness levels, plus USB-A and USB-C ports at 5V/2.1A. Its 230 degree flexible arm and 90 degree base axis let you fold it away or position it close to your book, which suits small tables.

The downside is the brightness range, because only three levels limits fine tuning, and folding hinges add moving parts that can loosen over time. It is lighter than the metal lamps here and may shift if you bump the table.

It stores flat in a drawer, which is useful for travel or a seasonal reading nook. Against the EJIAXIN, it adds touch controls and charging for a modest step up in price. Check that the hinges stay tight after a few weeks and fold it flat when you travel. It makes a good guest room lamp that can pack away between visits.
products.bestFor: Small tables and readers who like to fold a lamp away
pros: 230 degree arm folds and aims easily
Five light colors with touch control
USB-A and USB-C ports at 5V/2.1A
Compact when folded for storage
cons: Hinges may loosen with heavy use

products.name: EJIAXIN Flexible Gooseneck Table Lamp
products.description:
The EJIAXIN is the plain, no-learning pick. Its flexible gooseneck bends in any direction to put light on the page, and a forged iron body on a plastic base keeps it sturdy for the cost.

It has none of the electronics of the others, meaning no memory, no charging and a more limited choice of light, so it will not please anyone who wants fine control. It suits someone who wants a simple lamp that works without instructions.

Compared with the Dott Arts, it is sturdier and simpler but offers far fewer features. Keep it on a stable surface and bend the neck slowly to avoid fatigue in the metal. It is a sensible spare for a guest room or a hallway table.
products.bestFor: Readers who want a simple aimable lamp at the lowest cost
pros: Flexible neck aims light where needed
Forged iron build feels solid
No settings to learn
cons: No charging, memory or color options
Plastic base is lighter than metal

buyingCriteria.explanation: Older eyes need about three times more light than younger ones for fine detail, and AARP and Rensselaer guidance suggests at least 1,000 lux on the task. The LEPOWER at 800 lumens offers the most output, while the TROND gives seven levels and the Fitfull only three. Seated reading puts the lamp farther from the page than a desk lamp does, so extra output helps. Choose a lamp that can get bright for print and drop low for evening.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Controls you can use from a chair
buyingCriteria.explanation: A side table lamp is often reached at an awkward angle, so the control style matters. The BOHON has a rotary knob that you can find by feel, the TROND uses a swipe groove, and the Fitfull accepts a touch on its base or pole. For stiff or arthritic fingers, a knob or large touch target is easier than a tiny swipe zone. If you share the lamp with others, choose controls that need no explanation.

The American Lighting Association suggests 2700K to 3000K with CRI 80 or higher, while seniors guidance prefers 2700K to 5000K with CRI 90 or better. The BOHON spans 3000K to 5500K and the LEPOWER offers five color temperatures. Cooler light improves contrast for small print and warmer light relaxes the evening. Choose a lamp with both a warm and a neutral setting.

Glare sensitivity rises with age, and a bare bulb in view tires the eyes quickly. The TROND's light guide panel and the BOHON's 56 LEDs spread light to reduce hot spots, while the EJIAXIN's aimable gooseneck needs careful placement. Place the lamp beside and slightly behind you so the source is out of sight. A softer, wider source at a lower brightness often reads more comfortably than a small intense one.

An end table often serves as the charging spot for a phone or tablet. The Fitfull has an AC outlet with USB-A and USB-C, the Dott Arts offers USB-A and USB-C at 5V/2.1A, and the BOHON has a USB port. The LEPOWER and EJIAXIN have no charging at all. Count the devices you plug in nearby before you choose, because an outlet on the lamp frees a socket.

Side tables are small and often crowded with a glass or a remote. The LEPOWER's wide panel needs more room than the slim EJIAXIN or the folded Dott Arts, and a light plastic base can shift if bumped. Weight low down is safer than height, so look for a stable base. Measure your table and keep a hand's width free around the lamp.

howWeEvaluated.title: Brightness and dimming
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared output and the number of brightness steps from product specs. The LEPOWER leads at 800 lumens and ten levels, while the TROND offers seven and the Fitfull and Dott Arts only three. More range scored higher for both print and evening use.

howWeEvaluated.title: Controls and ease of use
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered knobs, touch panels and swipe grooves from a seated position. The BOHON's knob scored highest for reachability, while the TROND's swipe groove needs more accuracy. Lamps with memory or auto features gained points.

howWeEvaluated.title: Light quality and glare
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at LED count, panel design and color range. The TROND's light guide panel and the BOHON's 56 LEDs give even light, while the EJIAXIN relies on aiming. Lower glare and wider color options scored higher.

howWeEvaluated.title: Charging and features
howWeEvaluated.description: We counted USB ports and outlets. The Fitfull's AC outlet with USB-A and USB-C scored best, and the EJIAXIN and LEPOWER have none. Folding and memory features also counted.

howWeEvaluated.title: Build and value
howWeEvaluated.description: The EJIAXIN is the lowest cost with forged iron, while the TROND is the highest.

howToChoose.subheading: Knob and Swipe vs Touch Control

cards.label: Knob and swipe
cards.text: These give fine, repeatable control. The BOHON's knob and the TROND's swipe groove fall here. Choose them if you want exact brightness.

cards.label: Touch cycle
cards.text: These step through preset levels. The Fitfull and Dott Arts fall here. Choose them if you prefer one simple action.

howToChoose.note: Recommendation: the BOHON for most readers, the Fitfull if you want the simplest operation.

howToChoose.subheading: For Evening Tablet and Book Reading Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A warm setting for winding down, brightness that dims low, and a source that does not shine in your eyes. Use a lamp placed beside you rather than in front.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The BOHON's 3000K to 5500K range and memory suit evening use, and the TROND's seven steps give fine control. The Fitfull keeps a phone charging nearby.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You read daily and want even light, since the TROND's panel and the LEPOWER's output reduce eye strain. Spend more if you need both light and charging.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You read occasionally, where the EJIAXIN or Fitfull is enough. Save if you plan to move the lamp between rooms.

faq.q: How do I choose between a knob and a touch lamp?
faq.a: A knob like the BOHON's is easy to find by feel and gives smooth control. A touch lamp like the Fitfull steps through preset levels with one tap. If your hands are stiff, choose a knob or large touch area.

faq.q: How bright should a table reading lamp be?
faq.a: Guidance for older adults suggests about 1,000 lux on the page for fine detail. The LEPOWER's 800 lumens gives plenty of headroom. Use dimming to lower it for evening comfort.

faq.q: Is a more expensive lamp worth it?
faq.a: It can be if you read daily. The TROND's even light panel and the LEPOWER's higher output reduce strain. For occasional use, the EJIAXIN or Fitfull is adequate.
The BOHON senses ambient light and adjusts brightness automatically. It can be convenient, but it may change when another light is turned on. You can turn to manual control if you prefer.

faq.q: Can a foldable lamp be stable enough?
faq.a: The Dott Arts folds and has a flexible arm, but its hinges can loosen over time. Keep it on a flat surface away from the edge. A heavier base like the EJIAXIN's forged iron neck is steadier.

faq.q: How do I clean a lamp panel?
faq.a: Unplug the lamp and wipe the panel with a soft dry cloth. Avoid liquid cleaners on touch surfaces. Dust on wide panels like the LEPOWER's can reduce light, so wipe it every few weeks.
